title_guess: High-powered money: who issues India's currency, how much RBI may print (full reserve ideal vs the Minimum Reserve System), and how reserve money injected into banks multiplies (money multiplier, M0)
recurring_cast: brand_logo (RBI emblem coin) as the issuer at the left of every flow
rupee_note (green note with a rupee sign) riding an arrow out of the coin
funnel pouring into a light-blue BANKING SECTOR tray of eight small bank_building icons (opening, 231 s, 553 s)
vault (white safe labelled RESERVE) hung on a dotted line under the RBI coin
inverted blue cone labelled 'Reserve Requirement: 40%' sitting over the RBI coin
three-column ledger: Bank Reserves | RBI Reserve Req [40%] | Available for Lending
office_building (black tower) as the borrowing company
big '2.5 X' multiplier text over the banking tray
running_examples: ideal rule: to print 100 crore of notes RBI keeps 100 crore of gold and foreign exchange (100 Cr on the note and on the safe)
Minimum Reserve System, adopted 1956: at least Rs 515 crore = Rs 115 crore gold + Rs 400 crore foreign exchange; later struck to 200 crore with gold 115 crore 'or more' and a wider 'remaining amount'
spoken only: 150 crore gold + 50 crore treasury bills would meet the 200 crore minimum
Rs 1000 injected at a 40% reserve requirement: 400/600, 240/360, 144/216, 86.4/129.6 ... down to 0.52/0.78; reserves total 1000, loans total 1500, money supply up by 2500 = 2.5 X = 100/40
spoken only: at a 10% reserve requirement the multiplier is 10x and 1000 becomes 10,000
shown currency split: RBI notes 98% (shown, not spoken) vs Re 1 and coins 2% (spoken and shown)
reserve backing today '< 1%' of the currency in circulation (shown and spoken)

best_moments.why: a single note on the RBI-to-banks arrow appears to split into a row of four notes as 'ek ka chaar' is said (same event box as the four-note row seen at 561 s): multiplication of money as a picture, though the count does not match the 2.5x worked later

two stacked panels, blue 'Ideal scenario' (reserve = total value of currency) over grey 'In practice', where the '=' turns into a red '≠' as 'Minimum Reserve System' writes on: rule vs reality by flipping one sign on the same picture

the minimum reserve 'Rs 515 crore' is struck and '200 crore' written above it, a '+' appears after gold 115 crore, and the forex line is struck and replaced by a red 'remaining amount' list: a rule change shown on the numbers it changes
a '600 Rs Loan' arrow leaves the banking tray for a company tower, and an elbow arrow '600 Rs Deposit' brings it straight back into the tray: the loop that powers the multiplier in two arrows

ledger built round by round: each lending figure is bent back by an elbow arrow into the next 'Bank Reserves' row (+600, +360, +216) before it splits again 40/60: the cycle is visible, not only stated

the reserve column and the lending column light up blue and each sends an arrow to its total (1000, 1500); green brackets then join them into 2500 and a dotted arc links the circled 40% to the big '2.5 X': cause (reserve ratio) tied to result (multiplier)

weak_moments.why: a round inset shows a real banknote's printed promise clause with a real governor's signature; BIE must draw its own generic note and promise line
rule sentences as small blue text under the safe ('RBI required to keep same amount...', 'RBI empowered to issue currency to any extent...'); text carries the rule
doubtful claim to verify: '< 1%' backing and the spoken line that no real assets back the currency today; RBI is generally described as holding gold and foreign exchange far above the legal minimum

doubtful fact to verify: rupee securities and T-bills shown as part of the 200 crore minimum reserve (the minimum is usually described as gold plus foreign securities); the spoken 150 + 50 crore example is never drawn

doubtful definition: 'Reserve Money' tagged on all RBI-issued notes except Re 1 and coins (reserve money is usually defined as currency in circulation plus bankers' and other deposits with RBI); '98%' is on screen but never spoken
on-screen spelling error 'Total reserves held buy the banks'
the leakage condition (public keeps some cash) is a single text bullet; the spoken '1% or 2%' is not shown and nobody is drawn keeping notes
an app-promo overlay (phone, store badges) covers the list of M0's other names exactly while M0 is being named

segments.teaches: high-powered money is the money RBI pushes into India's banking sector; there it multiplies, 'one becomes four'

elements.what: 'HIGH POWER MONEY' under a green note
RBI emblem coin at the left
green rupee note on an arrow from the coin
coin → note → blue funnel into a light-blue 'BANKING SECTOR' tray of eight bank icons
the note on the arrow appears to become a row of four notes (event box matches the four-note row at 561 s)

segments.notes: 4 change events in 19 s. The title shows the term before any picture. Saancha: RBI coin → note → funnel → banking tray recurs at 231 s and 553 s. The 'one becomes four' row is an attractive picture but the video's own example gives 2.5x.
segments.idea: money RBI puts into banks grows into more money; this video shows how
segments.shown_as: a 'HIGH POWER MONEY' title sits under a green note; the RBI coin appears at the left and the note rides an arrow into a funnel that pours into a tray of bank icons labelled BANKING SECTOR; as 'multiply' is said the single note on the arrow seems to turn into a row of four
segments.example: 'ek ka chaar' (one becomes four), spoken and apparently drawn as four notes

segments.teaches: all notes from Rs 2 to Rs 500 are issued by RBI and called reserve money; Re 1 notes and coins are also put out by RBI but for the Government of India, and they are only about 2% of currency in circulation

elements.what: single green note at top
dotted line down to a list of denominations: Rs 500, 100, 50, 20, 10, 5, 2, Re 1, coins
light-blue band over Rs 500 to Rs 2; yellow band over Re 1 and coins
'Issued by the RBI' with the RBI coin and an arrow into the blue band
'Reserve Money' label on the blue band
GOVERNMENT icon (emblem with a group of people) → RBI coin 'Issued by the RBI' → yellow band (faded ghost first, then solid)
'98%' beside the blue band and '2%' beside the yellow band

segments.notes: 7 change events (~every 5 s). 98% is on screen but not spoken ('zyaadatar' is said). Doubtful definition to verify: 'reserve money' is put on RBI notes only; the standard definition of reserve money (M0) is currency in circulation plus bankers' and other deposits with RBI. The government-through-RBI path for Re 1 and coins is drawn as two arrows, which is a good 'on behalf of' picture.
segments.idea: almost all currency comes from RBI; small notes and coins come from the government through RBI
segments.shown_as: the canvas clears to one note; a dotted line drops to the list of denominations; a blue band covers Rs 500 to Rs 2 and an RBI coin labelled 'Issued by the RBI' points into it with a 'Reserve Money' tag; a faded issuer under it turns into a GOVERNMENT icon passing through an RBI coin into the yellow Re 1 and coins band; 98% and 2% label the two bands
segments.example: 98% RBI notes vs 2% Re 1 and coins

segments.teaches: can RBI print without limit? The stated rule: RBI may print only as much as it holds in reserve (100 crore of notes needs 100 crore of gold and foreign exchange); that is why every note carries the governor's promise to pay

elements.what: RBI coin at the left
long arrow labelled 'Issue' from the coin to a note
big '?' over the Issue arrow
white safe labelled RESERVE hung by a dotted line under the coin
blue rule sentence: RBI keeps reserve equal to the notes issued
'100 Cr' over the note and '100 Cr' beside the safe
'Gold' and 'Foreign Exchange Reserves' bullets beside the safe
round pink inset tied to the note by a line: close-up of a real note's promise clause in Hindi with a real governor's signature

segments.notes: 5 change events in 63 s (~every 12 s); long holds while the rule is explained. The '?' on the Issue arrow is a good 'is there a limit?' cue. The promise inset is a real banknote with a real signature: BIE will draw its own generic note and promise line.
segments.idea: in the full-reserve ideal, every rupee printed must be matched by a rupee of gold or foreign exchange kept aside
segments.shown_as: canvas clears to the RBI coin far from a note; an 'Issue' arrow with a big '?' joins them; a RESERVE safe drops on a dotted line under the coin with a blue rule sentence; '100 Cr' writes over the note and the same '100 Cr' beside the safe; 'Gold' and 'Foreign Exchange Reserves' list beside the safe; a round inset of the note's printed promise and signature hangs off the note
segments.example: 100 crore of notes ↔ 100 crore of reserve assets

segments.teaches: ideally the reserve should equal the total value of currency in the system; in practice it does not, and most countries follow a Minimum Reserve System

elements.what: safe with the RBI coin in front, labelled RESERVE
RESERVE '=' note, with 'Total value of currency in the system' beside the note
'IDEAL SCENARIO' over a light-blue panel holding the equation
'IN PRACTICE' over a grey copy of the panel
the grey panel's '=' turns into a red '≠'; '- MINIMUM RESERVE SYSTEM' writes on after IN PRACTICE

segments.notes: 5 change events in 22 s (~every 4 s), fast and clean. The two stacked panels are a reusable 'rule vs reality' saancha: copy the picture, change one sign.
segments.idea: full backing is the ideal; real systems back currency with only a minimum
segments.shown_as: the safe and the note face each other across a big '=' with 'Total value of currency in the system'; the pair becomes a blue 'Ideal scenario' panel, a grey copy slides under it as 'In practice', and in the grey copy the '=' flips to a red '≠' as 'Minimum Reserve System' writes on

segments.teaches: India adopted the Minimum Reserve System in 1956: RBI must hold at least Rs 515 crore (Rs 115 crore gold, Rs 400 crore foreign exchange) and may then print any amount; so reserves are below 1% of the currency today

elements.what: '[India adopted this system in 1956]' over the In practice panel, now alone at the top
dotted line from the safe down to a 'MINIMUM RESERVE' box
'Rs 515 crore' heading with bullets 'Gold - Rs 115 crore' and 'Foreign Exchange Reserves - Rs 400 crore'
blue rule sentence: RBI may issue currency to any extent if it keeps this minimum
curved blue arrow from the note back to the safe with a '< 1%' tag

segments.notes: 7 change events in 44 s (~every 6 s), each number written as it is spoken. Doubtful to verify: the '< 1%' claim and the spoken line that no real assets back the currency today (RBI's actual gold and forex holdings are much larger than the legal minimum).
segments.idea: a small fixed minimum of gold and forex lets RBI print any amount, so the backing is a tiny share of the currency
segments.shown_as: the ideal panel drops away and the grey 'In practice' panel moves to the top with a 1956 tag; a dotted line runs from the safe down to a 'Minimum reserve' box where 'Rs 515 crore', then gold 115 crore, then forex 400 crore write on with the words; a rule line writes under it; a curved arrow from the note back to the safe carries '< 1%'

segments.teaches: Indian currency became a managed paper currency; the minimum was cut to Rs 200 crore with gold 115 crore or more, and the rest may now include (as shown) rupee securities, foreign exchange and T-bills

elements.what: yellow 'Managed Paper Currency System' highlight tag above the panel
'Rs 515 crore' struck in red, '200 crore' written above it
red '+' after 'Gold - Rs 115 crore' (115 or more)
forex line and 'Rs 400 crore' struck; red 'Remaining amount: rupee securities, foreign exchange, T-bills etc.' written at the left, then moved into the box as a red tag row

segments.notes: 4 change events in 49 s (~every 12 s). Spoken but not shown: the what-if '150 crore gold + 50 crore T-bills meets the 200 crore minimum'. Doubtful fact to verify: T-bills and rupee securities counted within the 200 crore minimum (usually described as gold plus foreign securities). The year of the cut to 200 crore is not said.
segments.idea: the legal minimum was cut and widened, so the currency is managed, not backed
segments.shown_as: a yellow 'Managed paper currency system' tag lights above the panel; the 515 crore heading is struck and '200 crore' written over it; a red '+' appears after gold 115 crore; the forex line is struck through and a red 'remaining amount' list (rupee securities, forex, T-bills) writes in at the left and then takes the struck line's place
segments.example: 515 crore → 200 crore (gold ≥ 115 crore + remaining amount); spoken only: 150 gold + 50 T-bills

segments.teaches: RBI injects reserve money into banks through repo, long-term repo operations (LTROs), MSF and open market operations; if RBI injects Rs 1000, the banking sector's total reserves rise by Rs 1000

elements.what: RBI coin → note → funnel → BANKING SECTOR tray of eight bank icons (opening picture rebuilt)
the note on the arrow appears to become a row of notes again as 'ek ka chaar' is said, then returns to one
'Reserve Money' label over the note
'Injects:' list under the arrow: Repo operations, LTROs, MSF, Open Market Operations
'1000 Rs' over the Reserve Money label
italic note under the tray: total reserves held by the banks increased by 1000 Rs (spelled 'held buy')

segments.notes: 6 change events in 46 s (~every 8 s). The four tools are a recall list (already studied), text only. On-screen typo 'held buy'.
segments.idea: RBI's money enters banks as reserves through its lending and market tools
segments.shown_as: the opening coin-note-funnel-tray picture is rebuilt; the note briefly multiplies on the arrow; a 'Reserve Money' tag lands on it, an 'Injects:' list of repo, LTROs, MSF and OMO writes under the arrow, '1000 Rs' lands over the tag and a line under the tray says the banks' reserves rose by 1000

segments.teaches: with a 40% reserve requirement, banks keep 400 (as CRR and SLR) and may lend 600; a company that borrows 600 deposits it or spends it, and whoever receives it deposits it, so the 600 comes back to the banks

elements.what: inverted light-blue cone labelled 'Reserve Requirement: 40%' sitting over the RBI coin
'600 Rs Loan' arrow from the tray to a black office tower
black office tower (the borrowing company)
elbow arrow '600 Rs Deposit' from the tower back down into the tray

segments.notes: 3 change events in 65 s (~every 22 s); slow, voice-led. The 400 kept as reserve is spoken but not drawn here (it first appears in the ledger at about 359 s). The cash-in-hand leakage (322-341 s) is spoken only. '40% as CRR and SLR' is a simplification to flag: the textbook multiplier normally uses cash reserves.
segments.idea: lent money returns to banks as new deposits
segments.shown_as: a blue cone marked 'Reserve requirement 40%' settles over the RBI coin; a '600 Rs Loan' arrow runs from the banking tray out to a company tower, and an elbow arrow '600 Rs Deposit' loops from the tower back into the tray
segments.example: 1000 at 40% → keep 400, lend 600 → 600 returns as deposit

segments.teaches: the cycle round by round: 1000 → 400 kept, 600 lent; 600 returns → 240 kept, 360 lent; 360 returns → 144 kept, 216 lent; and so on

elements.what: small BANKING SECTOR chip at top left
three columns: Bank Reserves | RBI Reserve Req [40%] | Available for Lending, with tall dividers
elbow arrows from each lending figure back to a new '+' row in Bank Reserves (+600, +360, +216, +129.6)

segments.notes: 5 change events in 72 s, but each row writes on with its spoken number (every 5-10 s). Strong: the return arrow makes 'it comes back as a deposit' visible in the ledger.
segments.idea: each loan comes back as a deposit and splits again 40/60, so the amounts shrink round by round
segments.shown_as: canvas clears to a three-column ledger beside a small banking chip; '+1000' in Bank Reserves splits into 400 (reserve) and 600 (lend); an elbow arrow bends 600 back to a new '+600' row which splits into 240 and 360; the same bend and split repeats for 360 and 216 while the numbers shrink

segments.teaches: the cycle runs until nothing is left to lend (0.78 at the end); in all, 1000 goes into reserves and 1500 is lent

elements.what: Bank Reserves column cleared to '+1000'; the two right columns extended to 0.52 / 0.78
blue column band over all reserve figures with an arrow out to '1000 Rs'
blue column band over all lending figures with an arrow out to '1500 Rs'

segments.notes: 5 change events in 52 s (~every 10 s). The '+' rows and return arrows are cleared so the full series fits; summing a column by lighting it and pointing to its total is a clean move. Small rounding/format slips on screen ('+46.65', '+27.99' carry stray plus signs).
segments.idea: add up the shrinking rounds: 1000 in reserves and 1500 in loans
segments.shown_as: the deposit rows and bend arrows are cleared and both right columns run down to 0.52 and 0.78; the reserve column lights blue with an arrow out to '1000 Rs', then the lending column lights blue with an arrow out to '1500 Rs'
segments.example: sum of reserves 1000, sum of loans 1500; last lendable 0.78

segments.teaches: 1000 injected became 2500 in the banking sector; the result is a bit smaller in practice because people keep some cash, which does not return to banks

elements.what: 40% cone over the RBI coin; '1000 Rs Reserve Money Injected' arrow into a small banking chip
two-column summary: RBI Reserve Req [40%] 1000 Rs | Available for Lending 1500 Rs
two green brackets from 1000 and 1500 joining at '2500 Rs'
pale box: the banking system's ability to create deposit money depends on, with one bullet: the share the public holds as currency

segments.notes: 5 change events in 42 s (~every 8 s). The '1% or 2%' cash-held figure is spoken only; the leakage is one text bullet with no picture.
segments.idea: reserves plus loans add up to 2500 created from 1000, minus whatever people keep as cash
segments.shown_as: canvas clears to a compact line: 40% cone over the RBI coin, '1000 Rs reserve money injected' arrow into the banking chip, and a two-cell summary 1000 | 1500; two green brackets run down from both cells and meet at '2500 Rs'; a pale callout then lists 'portion the public holds as currency' as the limit

segments.teaches: money supply became 2.5 times: this multiple is the money multiplier, which depends on the reserve requirement; formula 1 / reserve requirement x 100 = 100/40 = 2.5; at 10% it would be 10x

elements.what: arrow out of the banking chip to '2500 Rs Increase in Money Supply'
big grey '2.5 X' above the banking chip
'Money Multiplier' label with a stroke to the 2.5 X
yellow circle around the 40% with a dotted arc from it to the 2.5 X
pink box: Money Multiplier = 1 / Reserve Requirement x 100, then '= 100/40 = 2.5'

segments.notes: 6 change events in 45 s (~every 8 s). The dotted arc from the 40% to the 2.5 X ties the cause to the result. Spoken only: the what-if '10% gives 10x, 1000 becomes 10,000'. The 'x 100' form needs the ratio written as a percent; '1 / 0.40' is cleaner.
segments.idea: the multiplier is one over the reserve ratio: 40% gives 2.5 times
segments.shown_as: the ledger cells and brackets give way to one arrow out of the banking chip to '2500 Rs increase in money supply'; a big '2.5 X' lands over the chip with a 'Money Multiplier' label; the 40% is circled in yellow and a dotted arc runs from it to the 2.5 X; a pink formula box writes on and is finished with '= 100/40 = 2.5'

segments.teaches: money RBI injects into banks can become four times or ten times depending on the reserve requirement; because it multiplies it is called high-powered money, also basic money, primary money or monetary base, written M0

elements.what: RBI coin → note → funnel → BANKING SECTOR tray (third time)
the note becomes a row of four notes on the arrow, then a single note again
dotted line down from the note to a list: High powered money, Basic money, Primary money, Money base
'M0' above the note
app-promo overlay (phone mock-up, store badges, course banner) covering the lower half

segments.notes: 6 change events in 47 s (~every 8 s). The spoken 'ek ka das' (one becomes ten) is not drawn as ten notes as far as the frames show. The promo overlay hides the list while M0 is named.
segments.idea: the money RBI injects is high-powered because it multiplies; its short name is M0
segments.shown_as: the opening picture returns: the note on the RBI arrow turns into a row of four notes and back to one; a dotted line drops from the note to its other names, and 'M0' lands above the note as a promo overlay slides over the lower half
segments.example: one becomes four (drawn), one becomes ten (spoken only)
